action_summary: The standing question asked whether one try -> permanent skill is solved and what the open limiting factor now is. This round answered by executing the loop instead of re-reading it, and by fixing the harness fault the execution exposed. Through the unified front door (solve_or_learn, learn=True) on the tracked bundle: a one-example teaching wrote a CHANGE_LEARNED_FROM_EXAMPLES_V1 lesson (teach pass, PASS__TIER0_COMPILED_SKILL_RECALL, 204.6 ms), and a second call edited a file created after the teaching (str(x) -> repr(x), same status) -- four executions, four passes across raw recall and the front door, stdout_equals verified, hit_count 2/2 in the live sqlite (the tracked bundle's exported hit_count stays 0; the sqlite is the counter, recorded as a measurement trap). The refusals were named: a coordinated rename example declined with 'cannot be repeated one place at a time'; learn=False skips Tier0 by design (already pinned elsewhere, verified before not re-pinning). The new front-door test then FAILED under a venv interpreter, and the failure was the harness: confine_v1.run() launched its helper with sys.executable, the helper chroots into a root that mounts only /usr /bin /lib /lib64 plus the project, and helper.py's own post-chroot spawn of the program raised FileNotFoundError before any program line ran -- every confined run exited 1 with a harness traceback that read like the taught program failing. Fix: _python_in_chroot() in confine_v1, the exact rule brokered_workspace_execution_v1 already follows (prefer /usr/bin/python3, /bin/python3, sys.executable only under a mounted prefix), applied at the helper launch so the helper carries a chroot-visible interpreter for both spawns. Pinned both ends: ChrootInterpreterTests asserts the launch argv never contains a venv interpreter, and the front-door test is the integration pin because it runs under the venv that failed on base. Siblings surveyed, deliberately not fixed: zero_ambient_namespace_launcher_v1 execs caller argv after chroot (creature_runtime passes sys.executable) -- same class, unmeasured, named next. Two candidate instruments killed by measurement before code: converting receipts' output_sha256 into expect_file_sha256 (only 28 records carry both argv and a digest, 25 unrunnable here, 3 runnable wrote to a cleaned parent -- would move ~3 records) and blanket expect_exit:0 on the 442 started passes (relabels without adding failure power; the audit already fails nonzero without it). State adjudicated with probes: THE_SYSTEM_ALREADY_WORKS's mechanism claims are true (4-tier entry demonstrated end to end; bundle/db/transfer/verify state present; auto-seed from the tracked bundle with content-sha, skill_id and ownership-receipt checks re-read and already pinned), while the skeptical line stands on the audit's 1.7% checkable fraction and on identification (one showing underdetermines: fresh-set diff/extra falsified; the rename refusal is the same boundary at engine level). Batteries after merging origin/main (03ac3628): confine+front-door+refactorings 103 passed 6 subtests; the other session's three new suites 72 passed; total 175 passed 0 failed this round; zero spend; tracked state restored after every learn=True run.
explicit_user_authorization: Owner directive 2026-11-12 (standing): determine what is real about instant learning and advanced coding/computer-use actions, kill bad ideas before implementation, think from first principles, maximize use of the latest 2026 research, and always push and merge completed work. This change is the harness-fidelity and front-door-pin half of that order: execute the one-shot loop through the production door instead of re-reading documents about it, repair the confinement launcher fault that made every confined run under a venv read as a program failure, and pin both ends. Zero-spend runtime repair with pins; no governance change; no capability credit; no sentience claim.
